title: A Primal-Dual Formulation for Deep Learning with Constraints
authors: Yatin Nandwani, Abhishek Pathak, Mausam, Parag Singla
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2019), Vol. 32
conclusions: Proposes a Lagrangian/primal-dual formulation for training deep networks subject to hard logic constraints defined directly over the network's output probability distributions (not just weights).

Constraints (arbitrary logical expressions over predicted labels) are converted to soft-logic value functions in [0,1], combined with a hinge so no penalty is paid once a constraint is satisfied, then enforced via one Lagrange multiplier per constraint type (reduces O(mK) multipliers to O(K)).

Solved via alternating min-max (gradient ascent on multipliers, gradient descent on weights) with a growing ratio of learning rates; proven to converge to a local min-max point (Theorem 1, via Jin et al. 2019 min-max theory).
Framework extends naturally to semi-supervised learning since constraints do not require target labels, only network predictions.

Experiments on SRL, NER+POS (multi-task), and fine-grained entity typing (TypeNet) show constrained training (CL) beats an unconstrained baseline and post-hoc constrained inference/decoding, especially in low-data regimes, and drastically reduces constraint violations (e.g., 3 orders of magnitude on TypeNet); in several cases CL alone matches or exceeds CL+constrained-inference, sometimes eliminating the need for post-hoc decoding altogether.
Compares favorably against a fixed soft-penalty baseline (Diligenti et al. 2017a) by avoiding manual search over a constant lambda.
